SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. S. B. D 148
Yangtzepoo Station,
REPORT
Date July 22nd. 1930.
Subject (in full) Re seizure of Communistic Literature at No.280.Thorburn Road.
Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I.Blenkinsop.

Sir,
At about 7.p.m. on the 22-7-30 a telephone message was received from C.D.C.181.Tsang Tuh Kung, to the effect that he had arrested a male Chinese and seized a quantity of coomunistic literature at No.280.Thorburn Road.
On receipt of the above information C.D.C.225.Zee Kwe Yong and myself immediately proceeded to the above address and there saw a male Chinese named "Bang Siau S Ts", native of Kompo, residing at 324.Dalny Road in the custody of C.D.C.181, together with a quantity of communistic literature and several copies of the "Shanghai Pau" newspaper, the sale of which is prohibited owing to its communistic attitude. I questioned C.D.C.181 and he stated that at about 6.45.p.m. on the 22-7-30, he happened to be passing No.280.Thorburn Road, when he saw the arrested person (Bang Siau S Ts) quarrelling together with the house tenant, one named "Wong Siau Yeu" (C.P.C.1226 attached to Yangtzepoo Police Station), and on asking the reason was informed by C.P.C.1226 that about ten days previously a female, name, etc unknown came to the above address and hired the front and middle upstairs rooms paying $9-70.cents room rent in advance, and in this room she had several stools and benches, which the arrested person stated he had been sent to remove, together with a small boy, who made his escape at the time the arrested person was detained.
Hearing the above news the C.D.C.181 decided to view the aforementioned rooms and whilst doing so found the aforementioned communistic literature and copies of the

Date July 22nd. 1930

Subject (in full) Re seizure of Communistic Literature at No.280.Thorburn Road.

Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I.Blenkinsop.

"Shanghai Pau".
I questioned the arrested person (Bang Siau S Ts) and he stated that he had met a boy named "Ling Kung", who previously worked together with him at the Kung Dah Cotton Mill (then the Oriental Cotton Mill), Yangtszepoo Road, about three years ago, in the Tah Woo Ka alleyway off Yangtszepoo Road together with a male Chinese whom he did not know, and these two persons asked him to accompany them to No.280.Thorburn Road, to remove certain pieces of furniture, which he did so, and was so arrested. He denies knowing anything about the communistic literature. He was accordingly removed to the Yangtszepoo Police Station for further enquiries.

At about 9.p.m. on the 22-7-30, a further telephone message was received from C.D.C.181 from No.280.Thorburn Road stating that he had arrested a male and female Chinese who had visited the above address, and he thought that they were communists. On receipt of this message D.S.Tilton, D.P.S.McPhee, myself and a party of Chinese detectives and uniform constables visited the aforementioned address and took into custody the two suspects.

Questioned at the Yangtszepoo Police Station by myself through the aid of an interpreter, the female one named "Hung Yeu", residing at No.1120.Pingliang Road stated that sometime ago she met a female named "Ah Moo" (whereabouts now unknown) on Thorburn Road, and she got into conversation with this female, who suggested that she learn Chinese characters, and asked her to visit her house at No.280.

Subject (in full) Re seizure of Communistic Literature at No.280.Thorburn Road.

about to do so this inst (22-7-30) was arrested.
The male Chinese one named "Wong Sing Ming", residing at
No.1120.Pingliang Road, stated that he saw a crowd collecting
outside No.280.Thorburn Road, and went there out of curiosity
and was arrested.
Both the above mentioned male and female denied
knowing anything about the communistic literature seized.
C.P.C.1226 questioned stated that he had not seen the
female who hired the room for at least the last three days,
and he also denied knowing that the two rooms were used for
communistic purposes, he also stated that the female occupy-
ing the said rooms always entered the house through the rear
door, and therefore he did not always notice when she left
or entered the premises.
Having no information that the three arrested persons
had any connection with the communistic literature these
persons were released after their addresses had been verified,
and Det.Supt.Robertson had been given the facts of the case.

I am Sir,
Your Obedient Servant,
J. S. Blenkinsop,
D.S.I.

一九三 年 月 日

Subjects for the General Strike of Cotton Mill Labourers.
The capitalists are ill-treating the labourers worse and worse.
The San Sing, Wei Tung, Ewo & Yangtszepoo Mills have changed the
3 or 5 day shift working system,and are continually dismissing
workers, in large numbers. The workers are having more work
and longer working hours. They are all in danger of being killed
by the machinery and drowned in water. Fellow workers, we can't
forbear these any longer. It is very urgent to call a general
strike at present. Fellow workers, all rise and do your best
to have the following articles materialised:-
1. The capitalists should not co-operate with the imperialist
Koumingtang to oppress the Cotton Mill Labour Union and its branch
unions, but recognise that the union has the authority to repre-
sent labourers and give a subsidy of $300 or $500 to the union
each month.
2. The capitalists should not co-operate with police detectives
military,or police to interfere with the freedom of workers inside
and outside the mills, or to arrest labourers or their leaders.
3. The capitalists should not co-operate with the Koumingtang,
labour thieves or running dogs to organise "yellow" labour union,
force workers to be its members and collect membership fee.
4. The capitalists should make all the arrested labourers
released and reinstate them.
5. A 30% increase in wages and $6 rice allowance.
6. The capitalists should not dismiss workers and reinstate
all those dismissed.
7. The capitalists should not put more work on labourers
by speeding the machines and cutting down the number of employees.
8. The capitalists should not enforce the 3 or 5 day/shift
working system, and if they do, a week's pay should be given to
labourers.
9. Female workers not to clean machines, sweep the floor
and cut the coarse yarn. 2 months leave be given for giving birth
to a child and 5 days leave for the monthly course period of woman.

Full pay be given for the period on leave.
10. Juvenile workers should not work as substitutes for
adults. When their training is accomplished, full wages be given.
The labour contractors should not cut their wages down for themselves.
11. Casual workers be paid the same as general workers and also
treated as general workers. They should not be dismissed without
cause.
12. Foremen should not assault or abuse workers. Workers
should not be fined. Cancel the photographing of workers and
the shop security for them. Better their treatments.
13. Memorial days and Sundays are holidays. Full pay for same.
15 minutes rest at 3 and 9 o'clock. Machines be stopped for one hour
for each meal. In summer, when the temperature is over 90 degrees,
work be stopped, but wages be given just the same.
14. The capitalists be held responsible for the safety of the
workers lives. Workers should not be put on work of a dangerous
nature.
The Shanghai Cotton Mills Labour Union.
1-7-30.

沙廠同盟罷工綱領

一，堅決反對帝國主義者及其走狗軍閥對工人的壓迫與剝削。
二，要求增加工資，改善待遇，實行八小時工作制。
三，承認工會代表權，不得干涉工會活動。
四，廢除包工制，禁止剋扣工資。
五，保障女工童工權益，實行同工同酬。
六，設立勞動保險，撫傷亡工人。
七，尊重工人人格，禁止辱罵毆打。
八，改善工廠衛生條件，提供清潔飲水。
九，允許工人集會結社自由。
十，罷工期間工資照發，不得開除罷工工人。
十一，簽訂集體合同，保障工人長期利益。
十二，成立勞資協調委員會，解決糾紛。
十三，政府應保護工人合法權益，懲辦違法資本家。
十四，本綱領自簽字之日起生效，雙方共同遵守。

上海紗廠工會
七月一日
